title: Launchpad: SDK + API orchestration for streaming, structured output, and function-calling samples
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Purpose: Coordinate a holistic launch runbook that delivers production-ready SDKs and API samples covering streaming responses, structured output schemas, and function-calling integrations. Scope: ship canonical examples for JS/Python/Go, a samples matrix for common integration patterns, release notes copy, and a cross-team rollout checklist. Goals: reduce integration friction for customers, ensure parity between SDKs and hosted API behavior, and provide canary tests and telemetry hooks for early regression detection.
acceptance_criteria: Canonical streaming sample implemented in JS and Python that demonstrates chunked events, backpressure guidance, and reconnect behavior
Structured output sample with schema validation example and sample dataset for developers to run locally
Function-calling sample demonstrating safe tool invocation patterns, input sanitization notes, and failure-mode guidance
Release notes drafted and signed off by Docs, Security, and Eng; included in SDK release page and API changelog
Samples published under samples.redwood.ai repo and referenced by quickstarts; sample matrix completed
Canary tests running in staging and alerting on latency/regression defined in Console dashboard
Migration guidance and breaking change checklist for existing SDK users
tasks: Draft release notes TL;DR and expanded sections (owner: Aisha)
Implement JS streaming example with server-sent event wrapper (owner: Dev: Lena Park)
Add structured-output JSON schema and validation demo (owner: Eng: Rohit Mehta)
Function-calling sample that integrates with a mocked external tool and shows graceful degradation (owner: Eng: Mateo Ruiz)
Create sample matrix CSV mapping use-cases to sample files and SDK support (owner: PM: Miguel Santos)
Coordinate doc review with Developer Experience and Security (owner: Aisha)
Prepare canary test harness and integrate with staging pipeline (owner: ENG: Priya Anand)
Produce quickstart video (30s) and 1-pager for sales enablement (owner: Design: Zoe Carter)
progress_updates: 2025-02-12: Ticket created following triage with DX and runtime teams. Initial scope reviewed in triage meeting.
2025-02-14: Decided to ship JS + Python first, postpone Go sample to follow-up sprint due to bandwidth constraints. (Trade-off: faster dev velocity vs broader initial coverage).
2025-02-15: Eng flagged a compatibility edge for streaming SDK when proxying with certain load balancers; added canary test to detect connection drop patterns.
2025-02-16: Docs provided schema registry pattern and recommended validation library (Ajv for JS). Incorporated into acceptance criteria.
2025-02-18: Security review prelim notes: recommend explicit guidance on tool invocation timeouts and retries; added notes to function-calling sample.
2025-02-20: Sample matrix draft uploaded; awaiting engineering links and PRs. Assigned canary test work to Priya.
rollout_plan: Week -2: Freeze API surface for samples; finalize schema and examples
Week -1: Merge sample PRs; deploy canary tests to staging; Docs publish draft
Day 0: Release SDK packages with sample pointers; post release notes; enable telemetry tags
Day +1: Monitor staging and production canaries; open rollback play if latency or regressions exceed thresholds
Day +7: Collect user feedback and telemetry; schedule follow-up patch for missing Go sample
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Streaming semantics differ between SDKs and hosted API causing developer confusion. Mitigation: include explicit compatibility table and end-to-end example harness.
Risk: Function-calling sample inadvertently encourages unsafe tool usage. Mitigation: include secure defaults, input sanitization patterns, and separation-of-privilege notes.
Risk: Late-breaking runtime change invalidates samples. Mitigation: run CI canaries against staging runtime and block release on failing regressions.
notes_for_engineering: Prefer non-blocking streaming examples that show reconnect and resume semantics rather than full-duplex websockets for MVP.
Instrument sample code with metrics tags (sdk.launchpad, sample.name, test-run-id) to surface adoption and failures in Console.
Keep sample dependencies minimal and pinned; include a Dockerfile for reproducible local runs.
